title: Pair Filters in an Extended Hubbard Model at Resonance
abstract: We investigate the dynamics of bound pairs in an extended Hubbard model at resonance. We show that a single fermion and a singlet bound pair possess identical dispersion relations and scatter off each other. In contrast, a neighboring doublon pair is dynamically pinned in the strong-interaction regime. Remarkably, a single fermion and a singlet bound pair exhibit fundamentally different scattering behaviors when encountering a pinned doublon pair acting as a scattering center. While the singlet bound pair undergoes perfect transmission, the single fermion is completely reflected. These results demonstrate that a neighboring doublon pair functions as an efficient filter that separates bound pairs from single particles. Numerical simulations fully support the analytical predictions. Our findings provide a dynamical mechanism for generating and manipulating bound-pair states.
summary: This work analyzes the dynamics of bound pairs in the extended Hubbard model, revealing that a neighboring double-doublon structure acts as a highly efficient, particle-selective filter. It predicts that single electrons are perfectly reflected by this barrier, while composite singlet bound pairs pass through unimpeded. This mechanism offers a theoretical pathway for controlling quantum transport in strongly correlated systems.
main_problem: Investigating the dynamics and scattering behavior of bound pairs (doublons) versus single fermions within an extended Hubbard model at resonance.
main_result: The double-doublon barrier acts as a particle-selective filter, allowing perfect transmission for singlet bound pairs while completely reflecting single electrons.
method: Theoretical derivation using effective Hamiltonians and confirmation via time-dependent wave-packet simulations.
model_or_system: The extended Hubbard model on a 1D chain, characterized by hopping ($\kappa$), on-site interaction ($U$), and nearest-neighbor interaction ($V$). The analysis focuses on the strong-interaction regime ($U, V \gg \kappa$) and the resonant condition ($V=U$).
key_observables: Reflection/transmission probabilities for single electrons and bound pairs; local particle density ($\langle n_e^j angle$); probability distributions ($P_e^l, P_p^l$).
important_parameters: Resonant condition ($V=U$), strong-interaction limit ($U \gg \kappa$), and the relative strengths of $U, V, \kappa$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on projecting the dynamics onto low-energy subspaces and treating the hopping term ($H_T$) as a perturbation in the strong-interaction limit.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the perfect reflection of single-electron wave packets and perfect transmission of bound-pair wave packets by the double-doublon barrier, demonstrating the filtering mechanism.
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives effective Hamiltonians for different scattering processes (e.g., electron + double-doublon, doublon + double-doublon) and uses wave-packet simulations to confirm the predicted particle-selective scattering behavior in the resonant regime.
why_interesting: The concept of a dynamically generated, particle-selective barrier is highly relevant for understanding engineered quantum materials or optical lattice setups where controlling the passage of composite excitations versus single particles is desired.
